title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Part III of the notes is 'Épinglages de Legendre des courbes elliptiques' (the cover sheet is on p.69). This page opens a digression titled roughly 'Épinglages of coverings by Kummer coverings and tangent épinglages (relative case)'. Its aim is to rigidify ('épingler') a tamely ramified cover over a cusp-section by tangent-vector data, uniformly over a base S. Presumably this is then applied to the Legendre-type level-2 cusps of elliptic curves.

Set-up:
- f: X → S is smooth of relative dimension 1, with a section t and X* = X \ t(S).
- One considers p: X' → X finite, with X' smooth over S of relative dimension 1 and a section t' lying over t.
- X' is 'modérément ramifié' at t' with index n. This means: étale-locally on X, near every point x' of t'(S), X' is isomorphic to the Kummer model X'_0 = Spec O_X[z]/(z^n − φ). Here φ is a local equation of the relative Cartier divisor t(S) near x = p(x').
- Marginal NB: n is NOT presumed invertible on S.

Why X'_0 is smooth over S for every n: locally X → A^1_S, given by φ, is étale. So X'_0 = X ×_{A^1, z↦z^n} A^1 is étale over A^1_S via z.

The canonical isomorphism (2), κ_{t'}: T_{X'/S,t'}^{⊗n} ≅ T_{X/S,t}:
- Dually it is (I'/I'^2)^{⊗n} ≅ I'^n/I'^{n+1} ≅ I/I^2 ⊗ O. Here I, I' are the ideals of t(S) and t'(S).
- It is induced by the relation φ = z^n, i.e. by the 'leading term' of the multiplicative ramification map, not by differentials (dφ = n z^{n−1}dz would degenerate).
- It does not depend on the choice of φ or z: changing φ to uφ forces z to change to u^{1/n}z.
- This is the relative, characteristic-free version of the classical fact for a tamely ramified extension of index e, namely (m'/m'^2)^{⊗e} ≅ m/m^2.

On the next page (p.71):
- G is a finite étale group scheme acting so that X'* is a G-torsor over X*.
- The stabilizer G_{t'} acts faithfully on the line T_{X'/S,t'}, giving a monomorphism (3) μ_n ↪ G. This is the canonical generator of inertia, defined via the tangent action.
- The torsor gives a class (4) ξ ∈ H^0(S, R^1 f°_* G).
- Proposition: (X', t') with its G-action is determined up to unique isomorphism by (2), (3) and (4).

In modern terms: a relative tangential-base-point / root-stack description of tame G-covers near a marked section. The data are the n-th root of the tangent line plus the inertia embedding μ_n ↪ G.
errors: The NB 'n not presumed invertible' is in tension with what follows. Once X'* is required to be a torsor under a finite étale G, the local model z^n = φ is étale over X* only where n is invertible: in characteristic p with p | n the Kummer model is inseparable over X*. Likewise a monomorphism μ_n ↪ G with G finite étale forces μ_n to be étale, i.e. n invertible on S. So in the torsor setting invertibility of n is automatic (a consequence) rather than an extra hypothesis. Only the bare definition and isomorphism (2) make sense for arbitrary n.

Minor: 'finis sur X' was originally written over S/X with corrections. The étale-local Kummer description implicitly assumes constant ramification index n along t'(S) (e.g. S connected). Neither is a substantive error.

ideas.what: Tamely ramified relative covers along a section are, étale-locally, Kummer covers z^n = φ (relative Abhyankar lemma)
ideas.modern_name: Abhyankar's lemma / tame ramification along a relative divisor; Kummer log-étale covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abhyankar; Grothendieck–Murre (1971); log version Fujiwara–Kato, Illusie
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. XIII (Abhyankar lemma); Grothendieck–Murre, LNM 208

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism T_{X'/S,t'}^{⊗n} ≅ T_{X/S,t} between tangent lines at a tame ramification section, valid in the relative setting
ideas.modern_name: n-th root of the normal/tangent line; tangent space of a twisted curve / root stack at a stacky point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for local fields (Serre, Corps locaux); relative/stacky form: Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli twisted curves (2003), Cadman root stacks, Wewers, Bertin–Romagny

ideas.what: Canonical embedding μ_n ↪ G via the action of the stabilizer of t' on the tangent line at t' (inertia with its canonical generator)
ideas.modern_name: Canonical generator of tame inertia / branch-cycle data; band of the μ_n-gerbe in twisted curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fried (branch cycle argument), Serre; stacky: Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli

ideas.what: Rigidifying ('épingler') covers by tangent data at a cusp-section, used for Legendre/level structures of elliptic curves
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points (relative); cusp rigidifications of Hurwitz/modular stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, P^1 minus 3 points); Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses base points at the boundary somewhat informally; unsure whether tangential

missed.claim: Around 1980–82 Grothendieck sets up, in the relative case over an arbitrary base S, rigidification of tame G-covers at a marked section by: an n-th root of the tangent line, the μ_n ↪ G inertia datum, and a class in R^1 f°_* G. This is essentially the data later encoded by twisted curves/root stacks (ACV 2003) and by relative tangential base points (Deligne 1989). Here it is aimed at Legendre épinglages of elliptic curves.
missed.quote: on définit un isom. canonique (2) T_{X'/S,t'}^{⊗n} ≅ T_{X/S,t}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows that the tangential-base-point and stacky-cusp formalism in the relative (moduli) setting was anticipated in Grothendieck's modular-curve work. This is mainly of historical interest; the mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the relative version of a standard tame-ramification fact plus inertia data. The early relative formulation (pre-Deligne 1989, pre-twisted curves) is historically notable but not mathematically novel to specialists today.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Épi-groupes' should be 'Épinglages'. The title reads roughly 'Digression: Épinglages de revêtements par [struck: revêtements finis lisses] rev. Kummeriens et épinglages tangents (cas relatif)'; 'lisses et gentils' is unlikely.
Margin NB: likely 'NB on ne présume pas n inversible sur S !!'.
'avec un degré de ramification n' — OK.
'loc. pour la top. étale sur X, X' est' — read 'X' est' (one occurrence of X'), not 'X, X', X''.
'via l'homo... locale' — reading uncertain; possibly 'via l'homomorphisme [norme] local', referring to the leading-term map z^n ↦ φ.
